svg.title: neobrutalism.dev — how it behaves, and how ours differs
svg.desc: Read from ekmas/neobrutalism-components: button.tsx, switch.tsx, tabs.tsx, accordion.tsx, checkbox.tsx, badge.tsx. Their behaviour first, drawn at their own values, then the eight places ours disagrees.

g.text: Their behaviour, read from their code.
ekmas/neobrutalism-components — button · switch · tabs · accordion · checkbox · badge. Drawn at their values, not ours.
The move the whole thing is built on
The button is pressed by looking at it.
It travels exactly its shadow's offset and lands where the shadow was —
the same grammar we use, but fired by the pointer arriving rather than by
a click. There is no :active rule anywhere in their button.
Four variants — three of them are about the shadow
stands off the page, presses in when addressed
the same move, without claiming to be the main action
lies flat until addressed, then pops out — translate −4 −4
and gains the shadow it did not have
for a control inside a box that must not move
FOUR SIZES, STATED IN THE CLASS
36 · 40 · 44 · 40 square — never left to the font
horizontal padding changes with the size; the frame never does
a black ring, outside, through a gap —
and the frame stays black too
the shadow survives, it just fades with everything else
transition-all — every property eases, nothing snaps
h-6 w-12, thumb h-4 w-4 with its own
the track eases colour, the thumb eases
the list is a box, h-12 with 2px and p-1;
the chosen tab is a filled box inside it
so choosing changes colour and nothing moves
Yes. It follows the WAI-ARIA pattern.
the header is filled with the accent, always;
open squares its bottom corners and the caret turns 180°
so the box does not change size
a badge has the frame but never the shadow —
it is a label, and labels are not pressed
on hover — the pointer presses it
a pointer crossing a toolbar would fire every button on the way
stays put, same gap — the fill firms up
the depth is the height; only a press may change it
ring-2 black, offset 2, over a black frame
the frame itself turns accent, no ring
a frame plus a ring is one event drawn twice
opacity fades the label with the frame and reads as broken
easing a 4px jump is the one soft thing in an idiom of hard edges
theirs vary the depth, ours vary the intent — a panel needs intent
lighter than the page in the dark theme
their dark background is a mid grey; ours is near black — 1.08:1
none — a tab fills, a button never holds
aria-pressed inverts and keeps its place
the panel has segmented ranges; a marketing kit does not
· reverse — a flat control that pops out when addressed. We have
nothing for a thing that should not look raised until you reach it.
· noShadow as a named variant rather than an exception per place.
· the switch's thumb carrying its own 2px frame — ours has none drawn.
· tabs as a framed box with a filled chosen tab, instead of a rule.
· press-on-hover — wrong for a dense panel, right for a landing page.
· the black focus ring over a black frame — two lines, one event.
· opacity for disabled — it fades the label along with the frame.
· transition-all — half a state easing while the rest snaps was exactly
and the black shadow in dark: 1.08:1 on our page
panel/public/reference-behaviour.svg — their behaviour read from button.tsx, switch.tsx, tabs.tsx, accordion.tsx, checkbox.tsx, badge.tsx.
Purple is theirs. Nothing here is implemented; the two panels above are the proposal.
